history.period: Built 1823 per most sources, but 1844 per others (conflicting; verify)
history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTION: the Rangji Temple is not in Ajmer town - it stands at Pushkar, district Ajmer, Rajasthan (~15 km northwest of Ajmer). This is the Old Rangji Temple (Purana Rangji Mandir), commissioned by Seth Puranmal Ganeriwal - a wealthy merchant of Hyderabad, said to be of Lakshmangarh in Shekhawati - and dating to 1823 (several travel sources) or 1844 (Triphobo and others); the date conflict is flagged. Pushkar has two Raghunath/Rangji temples (old and new). The temple is Pushkar's grandest example of South Indian (Dravidian) architecture - tall gopuram, fortified walls with chhatris and jharokhas, and frescoed outer parikrama depicting Krishna Leela, Ramayana and Samudra Manthan - blended with Rajasthani elements. The four-armed Venugopal (Krishna) idol is of black Kadappa stone from Tamil Nadu, flanked by Rukmini and Satyabhama. Sources conflict on the principal deity (Venugopal vs Garuda); the old-temple complex also houses Narasimha and Lakshmi. Note: some sources mention a 'Foreigners not allowed' sign historically seen at the old temple (verify current practice).

name: Rangji Temple
town_description: Pushkar is a small holy town in Ajmer district, Rajasthan, built around the sacred Pushkar Lake with over 500 temples. The Rangji Temple's Dravidian gopuram stands out among the town's Rajasthani-style shrines.

travel.airport: Jaipur International Airport is the nearest airport (~150 km).
travel.railway: Ajmer Junction is the nearest major railway station (~15 km).
travel.road: In Pushkar town, easily reached by road from Ajmer (~15 km); the temple is on Pushkar Road near Chhoti Basti.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, and during the Pushkar Fair (Kartik Poornima, October-November).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Typically open 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM with an afternoon closure, reopening around 3:00 PM (verify - sources differ); photography inside may be restricted.
